facts.text: Lenox Hill earned its name from a hill that once stood at 70th Street and Park Avenue, named after Scottish merchant Robert Lenox.
The neighborhood’s medical corridor anchors Lenox Hill Hospital, a 450‑bed facility founded in 1857 as the German Dispensary for immigrant communities.
In the late 19th century, the opening of the Fourth Avenue Tunnel buried the old steam railroad and spurred the construction of Beaux‑Arts co‑ops along Park Avenue.
Lenox Hill’s historic district, designated by the Landmarks Preservation Commission in 1981, protects many prewar buildings that line its tree‑lined streets.
The Lenox Hill Neighborhood House, founded in 1894, pioneered social services for immigrant families and set a precedent for community philanthropy in the area.
Topography shaped the neighborhood’s walkability, with residual slopes along cross‑streets creating varied pedestrian experiences amid its high‑rise density.
